significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would license the conclusion that retrieved facts precede a "content-general" late-layer gate whose state causally controls expression "without changing what was retrieved"—a form-(iii) ordering/invariance claim combined with a causal decomposition, establishing both the knowing-without-saying phenomenon and its mechanism. It would predict that failures induced by uncertainty and format mismatch converge on the same bottleneck and would separate retrieval from output control in the factual-recall pipeline studied by Meng et al. (2022), while connecting that pipeline to the directional behavioral control demonstrated by Arditi et al. (2024). Verified false would meaningfully reject a common late, low-rank gate in favor of content-specific or multiple mechanisms, although qualifiers such as "often," "many," and "under certain conditions" weaken determinacy at the margins; the central shared-gate and retrieval-invariance alternatives remain distinguishable. Topic-substitution check: the broad knowledge-retrieval topic alone would not earn this score—the asserted temporal ordering, cross-trigger common bottleneck, and retrieval-content invariance are specific constraints absent from a median localization hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "low-rank expression-control direction" and associated "gate activity," supporting a decode-time intervention that acts before the final answer rather than merely explaining an error post hoc, although the claim does not specify an automatic pre-query screen. After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion predicts a qualitative relation—late-layer gating should control expression while preserving retrieved content across uncertainty, atypical format, and different relations—rather than merely supplying an unconstrained search procedure, though it offers no quantitative cross-model law. Its asserted "content-general" scope covers multiple known-but-unsaid failure types, and the downstream users could include practitioners seeking to control factual output, subject to the acknowledged possibility of harming calibration or safety. Topic-substitution check: knowledge representations in general provide no such usable handle; the specific decode-time gate intervention and invariant retrieval/expression separation support reach above the topic median.
